$description: The pane's own chrome — region ⑦ (the context bar) and region ⑩ (the floating zoom pod), one mount per pane. It replaces `#tab-bar`, a 28px band styled identically to the tab strip above it that held five unrelated axes with no labels on any of them; the three axes here each say what they are, and the label is what stops the band re-accreting into an anonymous strip of chips. `panels/pane-context.ts` keeps every decision — which editor kinds a document declares, which canvas views it has, whether preview is a flag over them, what a lens may not write, which pane's stage a zoom verb lands on, and what a route param's candidate values are — and hands this document one projection of words, booleans and keyed rows. The bar and the banner share `[part="band"]` so the adapter can MEASURE what the stage must clear: a banner's height is its wrapped text, and only layout knows how many lines that is.

style.$description: The `.pc-*` rules of `styles/canvas.css`, keyed on `part` and carried here, plus `.jx-collab-banner` from `styles/shell.css` — the banner rides in this band and the rule rides with it. Three token repairs travel with them, the shape `surfaces/git-panel.json` describes: `--spectrum-font-size-75` and `--spectrum-font-size-50` resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document mounts outside it, so every rule reading one would silently have taken its px fallback; they are `--jx-text-md` (12px) and `--jx-text-sm` (11px) here, at the same values. Four rules are DELETED rather than moved because the kit already draws them: `.pc-derive-trigger`'s hand-built 22×20 box and its hover are `jx-action-button` quiet, `.pc-preview-toggle[selected]`'s four Spectrum custom-property overrides are the `emphasized` prop, and `.pc-ctx-manage:hover`'s underline is the only half of that rule worth keeping. The one rule ADDED is `pointer-events: auto` on the band, the pod and the popovers: `.pane-chrome` is `pointer-events: none` and gave it to its direct children through `.pane-chrome > *`, which a document root with `display: contents` is not — so the three surfaces that take the pointer say so themselves, which is also the honest place for it.

& [part=\"band\"].$description: The pane's top band: the bar plus the standing statements that must be readable before the first keystroke. One element so the adapter can MEASURE what the stage has to clear — a banner's height is its wrapped text, which only layout knows.

& [part=\"spacer\"].$description: What pushes the three axes right, and where §18.4's preset trigger goes. It stays in a lens, which draws no trigger: dropping it would move the one control a lens does draw.

& [part=\"axis-label\"].$description: The label is the point: five unlabelled controls on a 28px band is what this replaces, and the name is what stops the band re-accreting into an anonymous strip of chips.

& [part=\"editor-kind\"].$description: Capped so a long document name cannot push an axis off the end of a 28px band.

& [part=\"preview-toggle\"].$description: Not a third radio, and it must not read as one: it says the canvas is inert. The margin separates the two axes the eye is being asked to read as separate; the accent fill is the kit's `emphasized`, which is what deleted the four Spectrum custom properties this rule used to carry. The toggle is `quiet: false`, so it rests as a framed button of its own beside the framed View switch, as the Spectrum button did; quiet, it read as a fourth loose word once the switch beside it drew its frame.

& jx-action-button[part=\"preview-toggle.$description: The text padding the View switch's segments get from their group, which this toggle stands outside: the small size's 2px is for a glyph, and 6px is what the group gives a text segment. (0,3,1) outranks the kit's small padding at (0,3,0).

& [part=\"banner\"].$description: A standing statement, not an after-the-fact refusal: a guest without write access used to watch their edits apply locally and vanish at the publish gate. Inside the band the stage is offset by, so it pushes the document down instead of covering the one it is warning about.

& [part=\"pod\"].$description: Bottom-right of the pane, over the stage — a viewport control, which is not a document axis and so never belonged in a band beside one. It is a ROW of two controls and draws no box of its own: a 1px border and a 6px radius round 2px/4px of padding framed the zoom group's own frame and the Fit select's own frame, a frame inside a frame and busier than any other group in the chrome. Each control draws itself and takes `--pod-lift` to stand off the document under it, which is what the pod's fill and border used to do for both at once, and the gap between them says they are two controls rather than one strip with a seam. The right inset ADDS `--stage-scrollbar-w` because the chrome layer spans the whole cell, scrollbar gutter included: a fixed 12px put the pod 3px into Edit's 15px track, painting over it and swallowing its clicks. CSS cannot measure a scrollbar and this document cannot see the scroller, so `canvas/stage-scrollbar.ts` measures the stage's own and writes the width on the cell, where this reads it by cascade. It is 0 wherever the stage does not scroll or the scrollbar is an overlay. Physical right on purpose: Studio's chrome is never mirrored.

& [part=\"zoom-group\"].$description: The segmented frame floats on its own now that the pod draws no box around it. The radius is the one the first and last segments already draw, so the shadow follows the shape of the strip instead of a rectangle around it — the host's box IS that strip, since the group has no padding and each member's -1px pulls its own host in by a pixel.

& [part=\"pod\"] > [part=\"zoom-group\"].$description: One resting ink across the pod. A compact group rests its unselected members on `--jx-fg-dim` and brightens the chosen one, which is how a segmented control says which segment is on — and nothing in this pod is ever chosen: the three are a viewport verb, a readout and a verb. So the dim ink said nothing here and made `100%` read as disabled beside the Fit select's value, which is the same kind of readout at `--jx-fg`. (0,5,1) over the group's own resting rule at (0,4,1); the group's hover is (0,6,1) and still wins, which now leaves it only the wash.

& [part=\"zoom-label\"].$description: A floor under the percentage, so the pod does not shift as the value changes length. The width is the host's and the face is the control's, below: the control sets its own font and sits inside the host at its content width, so this rule used to carry a mono face nothing inherited and to open a 6px hole in the segmented frame before the `+` segment (measured: a 48px host round a 41.8px control, drawn in Inter).

& [part=\"zoom-label\"] > [part=\"contro.$description: The control fills its 48px host, closing the frame, and draws the percentage in the mono face with tabular digits so a changing value does not jitter. (0,3,0) outranks the kit control's own face at (0,2,0).

& [part=\"fit\"] > [part=\"control\"].$description: The pod's second control lifts off the document the way the first does, on the frame the kit's select already draws. On the control rather than the host, because the host is a column whose error region and help slot are the select's neighbours: the shadow has to follow the box that is painted.

& [part=\"popover\"].$description: Both panels take the pointer that `.pane-chrome` withholds. A popover is in the top layer while it shows, which changes where it PAINTS and not where it is in the tree, so it inherits `pointer-events: none` from the chrome layer exactly as the band does.

& [part=\"ctx\"].$description: One column of labelled groups over a footer that leaves for the definition site. This control only SELECTS (§2 principle 5) — nothing in it defines a breakpoint, a scheme or a feature query.

& [part=\"sizes\"], & [part=\"features\".$description: The two groups that WRAP, and the reason neither is a segmented control. A breakpoint or feature list is as long as the project makes it and this popover is a 240–340px column, so both fold onto a second line in any project with more than a few; a compact group cannot draw that — its seam is written in tree order, no selector can find the ends of a flex line, and it therefore refuses to wrap and would overflow the column instead (ui.md §5.4). Chips instead: each member draws its own rounded frame (`quiet: false`, since the group no longer frames it) and the chosen one takes the accent edge below. The gap is --jx-space-2 rather than the group's own 2px, which puts every small chip's hit area at the 24px floor on both axes instead of the 22px two overlapping extensions leave (§4.3).

& [part=\"sizes-item\"][data-selected] >.$description: A chosen chip reads the way a chosen segment does: the accent tint with an accent EDGE. A member's own selected state is a 15% tint over its neutral border, which among framed neighbours reads as a faint wash rather than as the one that is on — the measurement that gave the compact group its selected rule, restated here at the one place the group does not draw it. (0,4,0) over the member's own (0,3,0).

& [part=\"fields\"].$description: The fields, stacked. They were a row on the bar capped at 140px; in the popover each takes the full column so a route value or a JSON test prop is readable while you type it.
